task: Certify project MCP servers at protocol level
problem: Prove that Graphify and Context7 start, expose valid read-only tools, execute real calls, and fail safely without trusting configuration presence.

evidence: Graphify certification tested the CLI but not the MCP transport
Context7 certification validated evidence contracts but not the live MCP protocol
no repository MCP Inspector or protocol test harness existed

functional_fit.solves_required_problem: Yes; startup, inventory, schema, call, and negative-control probes passed.
functional_fit.unnecessary_features: The package includes a web UI, but certification invokes only its CLI.

project_fit.compatible_with_current_stack: Supports Node 24 and existing stdio MCP configuration.
project_fit.integration_surface: One pinned development dependency and one certification script.
project_fit.architecture_alignment: Tests existing servers without becoming a runtime control plane.

maturity.maintenance_activity: Official modelcontextprotocol organization with multiple maintainers.
maturity.documentation_quality: Official CLI documentation covers read-only config and tools/list/tools/call.
maturity.tests: Pilot exercised Graphify and Context7 plus an invalid tool.
maturity.production_usage_signal: Protocol reference tool; used only in development/CI.

security.security_history: No pilot finding; dependency audit remains required.
security.permissions_required: Only the permissions exposed by the selected MCP server.
security.secret_handling: No secrets supplied in this certification.
security.network_access: Context7 makes its existing documentation request; Graphify remains local.
security.supply_chain_risk: Pinned package has a substantial transitive tree including a deprecated legacy transport package.

ownership.maintainer_bus_factor: Seven npm maintainers and official organization ownership.
ownership.upgrade_cost: Version upgrades require rerunning seeded probes.
ownership.exit_strategy: Remove the dev dependency and certification script or replace with another protocol-level standard client.

operations.runtime_cost: Approximately 9-27 seconds per server probe on the Windows pilot.
operations.hosted_service_required: None beyond the already-used Context7 API.
operations.observability: Structured JSON report with durations, inventories, warnings, and failures.

engineering_cost.install_cost: Pinned development dependency plus Graphify's version-matched MCP extra.
engineering_cost.custom_build_cost: Higher and would duplicate protocol client/error handling.
engineering_cost.long_term_maintenance_cost: Bounded to the certification script and version refresh.

agent_fit.context7_support: Not needed for the protocol client itself.
agent_fit.deterministic_testability: Yes, except Context7 network availability is an explicit service dependency.

selected_candidate.name: @modelcontextprotocol/inspector
reason: caught the missing Graphify MCP optional runtime
proved real tool inventory and calls

rejected_candidates.name: Configuration-presence check
rejected_candidates.reason: would have falsely passed while graphify-mcp was unable to import its MCP runtime

rejected_candidates.name: Custom JSON-RPC client
rejected_candidates.reason: duplicates a maintained official protocol tool and increases test-harness ownership

risks: Context7 4.0.2 emits a Windows libuv teardown assertion after valid output
Inspector includes a deprecated legacy transport dependency
live Context7 certification depends on network availability
rollback_or_exit_strategy: retain host MCP configuration and use an equivalent standard protocol client

rounds.scope: existing project and native MCP capability
rounds.material_gain: proved no protocol harness existed and exposed Graphify's missing optional MCP runtime
official Inspector passed real inventories, calls, and deterministic negative control
